Compare categorical compositions across groups.

Source: R/compare-group-compositions.R
CompareGroupCompositions.Rd

Tests whether between-group Hellinger distances exceed within-group distances using a permutation null or conjugate Dirichlet posterior-predictive Bayes. Always reports an omnibus statistic. When contrasts is omitted, also tests every pairwise group comparison; when contrasts is supplied, those specifications are the contrast family (auto pairwises are omitted unless includePairwise = TRUE).

Usage

CompareGroupCompositions(
  x,
  method = c("permutation", "bayes"),
  contrasts = NULL,
  nPermutations = 1000,
  nPosterior = 100,
  nCores = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  priorPseudocounts = 1/2,
  pAdjustMethod = "holm",
  credibleInterval = c("hpdi", "cpi"),
  includePairwise = NULL,
  nope = "shuffle",
  energyNope = "shuffle",
  nNopeShuffles = 200,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A CategoryComposition object or long counts table.

method

Inference method: "permutation" or "bayes".

contrasts

Planned comparisons, or NULL for every pairwise contrast. A length-2 character vector is one pairwise comparison. A list may mix length-2 character vectors and lists with collapse (named remap of group levels) and/or groups (subset to these levels before testing). Names become contrastId values; unnamed elements get A_vs_B identifiers.

nPermutations

Number of label permutations (permutation method only).

nPosterior

Number of posterior draws (bayes method).

nCores

Number of parallel workers (default 1).

seed

Random seed for reproducibility.

priorPseudocounts

Jeffreys prior increment per category (default 1/2).

pAdjustMethod

Multiple-testing adjustment for permutation contrasts ("holm", "BH", "none"). Ignored for Bayes.

credibleInterval

Bayes interval type: "hpdi" (default, shortest 95% interval on the draws) or "cpi" (equal-tailed 2.5%/97.5% quantiles). Ignored for permutation.

includePairwise

Include every pairwise comparison in addition to contrasts. Default NULL includes pairwises when contrasts is omitted (the usual all-pairs analysis) and skips them when contrasts is supplied so Holm is paid only on the planned family. FALSE skips auto pairwises even when contrasts is omitted (omnibus only). TRUE keeps all pairwises even when contrasts is supplied (the old additive overlay).

nope

Bayes NOPE interval on \(R\). "shuffle" (default) sets a permutation-calibrated null reference interval whose upper bound comes from label shuffles within each posterior draw. A single number above 1 sets a fixed NOPE bound on \(R\) that you choose in advance. Either adds R_PPGTnope, R_nopeHigh, and R_hdiAboveNope to the output. "none" drops them. Ignored for permutation.

energyNope

Bayes NOPE interval on the energy distance \(E\), in squared Hellinger units. "shuffle" (default) sets a NOPE interval from the same label shuffles as nope. A single number above 0 sets a fixed NOPE bound on \(E\); ComputeEnergyNopeBound() turns a composition shift into one. Either adds E_PPGTnope, E_nopeHigh, and E_hdiAboveNope to the output. "none" drops them. Ignored for permutation.

nNopeShuffles

Label shuffles per posterior draw used to set the NOPEs (default 200). Each shuffle builds one group summary per shuffled statistic, so cost scales as nPosterior * nNopeShuffles summaries per contrast for one NOPE and twice that for both. Used only when method = "bayes" and nope or energyNope is "shuffle".

...

Ignored.

Value

A HellingerEnrichmentResult with omnibus summary, contrast table, and (Bayes only) long-format posterior draws including the omnibus draws. Bayes summaries carry R_PPGTnope, R_nopeHigh, and R_hdiAboveNope unless nope = "none", E_PPGTnope, E_nopeHigh, and E_hdiAboveNope unless energyNope = "none" (each edge column is the median across draws of the per-draw upper edge; each *_hdiAboveNope is TRUE when the 95% HPDI sits entirely above that reported edge), and enoughShufflesForNope when nope or energyNope is "shuffle" (FALSE when groups are too small for the NOPE, which is why the NOPE probabilities and HDI logicals are then NA); draws carries the per-draw R_nopeHigh and E_nopeHigh. Both methods carry energyDistance beside the ratio effectSize; Bayes adds energyCiLow/energyCiHigh and per-draw energyDistance in draws.

Details

The between/within Hellinger ratio, Jeffreys softening, observed-inclusive label-permutation p-value, and collapse/subset contrasts follow Paul Edlefsen's original procedure. method = "bayes" instead draws subject compositions from a conjugate Dirichlet posterior, rebuilds the Hellinger ratio \(R\) on each draw, and reports the posterior probability that \(R > 1\) (PPGT1) with a 95% highest posterior density interval on \(R\) by default.

PPGT1 alone overstates enrichment when counts are deep. The Dirichlet posterior only describes count noise within each subject, so as depth grows it concentrates on the sample \(R\), which is rarely exactly 1 even when groups do not differ. With nope = "shuffle" (the default), the package reports a Null-Oriented Permutation Equivalence (NOPE) interval on \(R\): a permutation-calibrated null reference interval for conditional effects. Within each posterior draw, the package shuffles group labels on that draw's own distance matrix, so the interval is conditional on the observed design (group sizes, depths, within-group spread) and on that draw's compositions. The goal parallels a permutation test, but NOPE reports a region instead of a p-value. The NOPE interval for \(R\) runs from 1 to the 95th percentile of the shuffled \(R\); R_nopeHigh is the median of that upper bound across draws, and R_PPGTnope is the posterior probability that \(R\) clears it. energyNope = "shuffle" (also the default) builds the matching interval for the energy distance \(E\) from the same shuffles, from 0 to E_nopeHigh, and reports E_PPGTnope.

NOPE borrows the equivalence logic of Kruschke's region of practical equivalence (ROPE) and changes two things. In Kruschke's procedure the analyst fixes the region before seeing the data, from domain knowledge of which effects are negligible, and the decision compares the 95% highest density interval with that region. Few analysts have that intuition for a ratio of Hellinger distances or an energy distance, so NOPE takes its upper bound from the data: the largest value of the statistic these subjects routinely produce when labels carry no information. The bound also differs from draw to draw, and each NOPE probability counts the draws that clear their own bound. R_hdiAboveNope and E_hdiAboveNope report Kruschke's comparison against the reported region: TRUE when the 95% HPDI sits entirely above that statistic's NOPE (effectCiLow > R_nopeHigh, energyCiLow > E_nopeHigh). The HPDI is the credible interval; the NOPE is the null region. When you know the smallest effect that matters, pass it as a fixed NOPE bound, which plays the role of Kruschke's preset region: nope = <number above 1> on \(R\), or energyNope = <number above 0> on \(E\) in squared Hellinger units. A fixed bound needs no shuffles, so it also works for groups too small for a NOPE interval.

To set a fixed bound on \(E\) from a composition shift, pass the reference and shifted compositions to ComputeEnergyNopeBound and hand its result to energyNope. It returns \(2(1 - \mathrm{BC})\), with BC the Bhattacharyya coefficient between the two compositions, which equals \(E\) when every subject sits at its group's mean and approximates it otherwise.

Because shuffling keeps the observed group sizes, depths, and within-group spread, the NOPE widens or narrows with the data rather than relying on a fixed number. Each draw's edge never falls below the no-difference value (1 for \(R\), 0 for \(E\)), so R_PPGTnope <= PPGT1 always holds, and E_PPGTnope never exceeds the posterior probability that \(E > 0\). Reading a NOPE probability above 0.95 asks that nearly every draw clear its own 95th shuffle percentile, which runs well below a 5% false-positive rate and costs power; a looser threshold such as 0.5 behaves more like the permutation test. The sampling-depth vignette measures both. Very small groups limit the NOPE the same way they limit the permutation p-value. With 3 versus 3 subjects there are only 10 distinct splits, so the true split alone is 10% of all shuffles and neither statistic can clear its 95th percentile. Whenever the true split is at least 5% of shuffles (e.g. 2 versus 2, 3 versus 3, 2 versus 4), the function sets each NOPE probability to NA with a warning rather than a misleading 0, and enoughShufflesForNope is FALSE so the reason travels with the result; 4 versus 4 (35 splits) is the smallest balanced design that supports it.

Both methods also report the energy distance between groups (energyDistance): twice the mean between-group squared Hellinger distance minus each group's mean within-group squared distance, averaged over group pairs for the omnibus. Squaring the existing distance matrix costs nothing extra. \(R\) measures how far apart the groups are relative to how spread out they are; \(E\) measures the shift in mean composition itself, as the squared distance between group centroids in square-root composition space, with no division. Independent count noise adds equally to between- and within-group squared distances and cancels from \(E\) in expectation, but Jeffreys softening and the curvature of the square root still shrink \(E\) at shallow depth, though less than they shrink the excess of \(R\) over 1 (see the sampling-depth vignette). \(E\) responds mainly to shifts in mean composition; a difference in spread alone moves it only slightly, likely through that same curvature. The sample estimate excludes each subject's distance to itself, so it can dip slightly below 0 when groups do not differ. The p-values and PPGT1 stay on \(R\); under Bayes the package reports a posterior interval on \(E\) (energyCiLow, energyCiHigh) and, with energyNope, E_PPGTnope and E_hdiAboveNope.
